title: host_declarations
description: What only the host repository knows and the toolkit cannot derive: the release-tag pattern, the setup command, the paths left out of the code-tree id and where each third-party version is declared in the repository. One file per host, spec/common/host_declarations.json, written by hand; every key is optional and a host that does not have the file keeps working.

$schema.description: JSON Schema URI identifying the schema this file conforms to: vc:host-declarations.

release_tag_pattern.description: Regular expression a git tag must match to count as a release tag. Decision rule: write the pattern of the tags your release process creates, anchored at both ends. Correct: '^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'. Anti-pattern: an unanchored pattern such as 'v1', which also matches candidate tags like 'v1.0.0-stage'.

setup_command.description: Shell command that prepares a clean checkout to run the verification commands (install dependencies, build generated sources). Decision rule: the one command a new contributor runs before the first test. Correct: 'npm ci'. Anti-pattern: a command that also starts services or runs tests.

code_tree_exclusions.description: Git pathspecs left out of the code-tree id, so a change under them does not invalidate recorded evidence. Decision rule: list what is not the product's own code and changes without changing behaviour. Correct: the toolkit submodule path, generated report folders. Anti-pattern: a source folder of the product, which would let evidence outlive a code change.

items.description: One git pathspec, relative to the repository root. Example: 'devspec_toolkit' or 'test-results/'.

pin_sources.description: Where the repository declares the version of each third party, keyed by the id of its third-party node. Every listed source must equal the pin of the node. Decision rule: list the files the build or deploy reads the version from (a lock file, a manifest, a version constant in code). A third party with no entry is not checked.

propertyNames.description: Id of a third-party node, as step 02 declares it. Example: 'tp-argon2'.

additionalProperties.description: The sources of one third party; all must equal its pin.

oneOf.description: A value read from a JSON file by an RFC 6901 JSON pointer.

type.description: Source type: the value is the string the pointer selects in the JSON file.

file.description: Path of the JSON file relative to the repository root. Example: 'package-lock.json'.

pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON pointer into the file; '~1' stands for '/' and '~0' for '~' inside a key. The pointer must select a string. Example: '/packages/node_modules~1argon2/version'.

oneOf.description: A value read from a text file by a regular expression.

type.description: Source type: the value is the capture group of the first match of the pattern in the text file.

file.description: Path of the text file relative to the repository root. Example: 'src/mail/client.ts'.

pattern.description: Regular expression with exactly one capture group; the first match in the file gives the value. Compiled in multi-line mode, so '^' and '$' match at the start and end of each line, as in the output guard of a binding. Example: 'MAILRELAY_API_VERSION = "(api-v[0-9]+)"'.
